sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Cocidius was a god of the north of Roman Britain, honoured by soldiers along Hadrian's Wall. Some twenty stones bear his name; five join him to the war god Mars, one altar to Silvanus, god of the woods, shown as a hunter with a dog and a stag. An inscription gives him the title Riocalatis with Teutates; another links him to Vernostonus. Two silver plaques show him with spear and shield. His name may not be Celtic; its ending could match a Welsh word for reddish, tied to 'red god' Da Derga.

okr.objective: Cocidius was a northern British god honoured by Roman soldiers and linked to Mars, Silvanus, and other deities.
key_results: About twenty inscriptions in Roman Britain carry his name.
He was equated with Mars, Silvanus, Teutates, and Vernostonus.
Altars depict him as both hunter and warrior.
His name may derive from a Welsh word meaning reddish.
